title: Asteroids, Comets, Planetary Rings and Small-Body Dynamics as Tests of the Frame

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Giorgia Nikolaidis, and this is Asteroids, Comets, Planetary Rings and Small-Body Dynamics as Tests of the Frame. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Giorgia Nikolaidis, and this is Asteroids, Comets, Planetary Rings and Small-Body Dynamics as Tests of the Frame. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Active Asteroids and Mass Loss Without Ice: Recoil and Dust Production for a Phaethon-Scale Body'. Its stated result: The deposited calculation gives the headline values mass_kg = 1.74e+14; dv_per_orbit_mm_s = 0.29; mean_accel = 6.38e-12. These values were computed from the stated inputs in compute.py, are reproduced in results.json, and support the paper's comparison with published small-body observations and its stated bound on any torsion-type correction at small-body densities.
Now we go one step further into the material.

'Asteroid Family Ages from Yarkovsky Spreading: The Width of a Family in Semimajor Axis as a Clock'. Its stated result: The deposited calculation gives the headline values age_2km_Myr = 250; age_5km_Myr = 625; dadt_2km = 2e-04. These values were computed from the stated inputs in compute.py, are reproduced in results.json, and support the paper's comparison with published small-body observations and its stated bound on any torsion-type correction at small-body densities.
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Binary Asteroid Evolution Under Tides and BYORP: Competing Timescales for a Kilometre-Scale Pair'. Its stated result: The deposited calculation gives the headline values mean_motion = 1.47e-04; t_change_kyr_at_5cm_yr = 0; separation_km = 1.18. These values were computed from the stated inputs in compute.py, are reproduced in results.json, and support the paper's comparison with published small-body observations and its stated bound on any torsion-type correction at small-body densities.
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Rings Around Small Bodies: Stability Distances for the Chariklo and Haumea Ring Systems'. Its stated result: The deposited calculation gives the headline values roche_chariklo_km = 313; ring_chariklo_km = 391; roche_haumea_km = 2509; ring_haumea_km = 2285. These values were computed from the stated inputs in compute.py, are reproduced in results.json, and support the paper's comparison with published small-body observations and its stated bound on any torsion-type correction at small-body densities.
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Comet Non-Gravitational Accelerations from Water-Ice Sublimation: Recoil Magnitudes for a Kilometre Nucleus'. Its stated result: The deposited calculation gives the headline values mdot_kg_s = 300; thrust_N = 4.50e+04; accel = 2.24e-09; accel_rel_solar_grav = 3.77e-07. These values were computed from the stated inputs in compute.py, are reproduced in results.json, and support the paper's comparison with published small-body observations and its stated bound on any torsion-type correction at small-body densities.
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'Comet Nucleus Tensile Strength Inferred from Rotation and Tidal Breakup: Pascal-Scale Cohesion'. Its stated result: The deposited calculation gives the headline values sigma_12h_2km_Pa = 25; sigma_5h_1km_Pa = 37. These values were computed from the stated inputs in compute.py, are reproduced in results.json, and support the paper's comparison with published small-body observations and its stated bound on any torsion-type correction at small-body densities.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Active Asteroids and Mass Loss Without Ice: Recoil and Dust Production for a Phaethon-Scale Body”. Its stated result is: The deposited calculation gives the headline values mass_kg = 1.74e+14; dv_per_orbit_mm_s = 0.29; mean_accel = 6.38e-12. These values were computed from the stated inputs in compute.py, are reproduced in results.json, and support the paper's comparison with published small-body observations and its (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Active Asteroids and Mass Loss Without Ice: Recoil and Dust Production for a Phaethon-Scale Body'; 'Asteroid Family Ages from Yarkovsky Spreading: The Width of a Family in Semimajor Axis as a Clock'; 'Binary Asteroid Evolution Under Tides and BYORP: Competing Timescales for a Kilometre-Scale Pair'; 'Rings Around Small Bodies: Stability Distances for the Chariklo and Haumea Ring Systems'; 'Comet Non-Gravitational Accelerations from Water-Ice Sublimation: Recoil Magnitudes for a Kilometre Nucleus'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.

questions.walk: Walk it through with me, step by step. questions.q: In the lesson, the paper 'Active Asteroids and Mass Loss Without Ice: Recoil and Dust Production for a Phaethon-Scale Body' reported a number for headline values mass_kg. What number did it report?
questions.why: You are doing this because a number you can produce from memory — and defend — is worth ten you have only seen glide past.
